question: As per the contents mentioned in Asokan inscriptions, how many major political centres were there in the Mauryan empire?
solution:
The correct answer is__** five.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the contents mentioned in Asokan inscriptions, there were** five major political centres **in the **Mauryan empire.** 
 
• The five major political centres of the Mauryan empire were located at** Pataliputra, Taxila, Ujjain, Tosali and Suvarnagiri.**
 
• **Pataliputra:-**
 
 
• It was the capital of the Mauryan empire.
 
• It was located on the Ganges River, and it was a major center of trade and commerce.
 
• Pataliputra was a well-planned city with a grid layout and a variety of public buildings, including palaces, temples, and gardens.
 
 
 
• **Taxila:-**
 
 
• It was located in the northwest of the Mauryan empire, and it was a major center of learning and culture.
 
• Taxila was home to a number of universities and schools, and it was a popular destination for students from all over the world.
 
 
 
• **Ujjain:-**
 
 
• It was located in the central part of the Mauryan empire, and it was a major center of trade and commerce.
 
• Ujjain was also a major religious center, and it was home to a number of temples and shrines.
 
 
 
• **Tosali:-**
 
 
• It was located in the east of the Mauryan empire, and it was a major center of agriculture and commerce.
 
• Tosali was also a major port city, and it played an important role in the empire's trade with other countries.
 
 
 
• **Suvarnagir:-**
 
 
• It was located in the south of the Mauryan empire, and it was a major center of gold mining and trade.
 
• Suvarnagiri was also a major religious center, and it was home to a number of temples and shrines.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asokan inscriptions:-**

 
 
• These are a collection of more than 30 edicts issued by Emperor Ashoka of the Maurya Empire (272-232 BCE).
 
• They are found on rocks and pillars throughout India, Nepal, Pakistan, and Afghanistan.
 
• They are written in a variety of languages, including Prakrit, Brahmi, Aramaic, and Greek.
